findings.title: Denial cache keeps a creator denied on a just-created resource for the full TTL
findings.body: Check() caches a denial keyed by user, action, name and parent folder for shortCacheTTL (30s) whenever the check is denied (line ~154). The PR's stated purpose is to let a dashboard/folder creator access the resource they just created. If a check for a not-yet-existing resource is denied, the denial is cached. When the resource is created and the permission is granted, the next Check hits the denial cache at line 117 and returns Allowed=false before any permission lookup. Access is therefore still refused for up to 30 seconds, so the reported bug is not fixed. The denial entry is also never invalidated when permissions change. Consider not caching denials for resources that may be newly created, or bypassing the denial cache when the permission set is refreshed.

findings.title: No test covers the actual regression scenario (deny, then grant, then allow)
findings.body: TestService_CacheCheck only checks that a pre-seeded denial entry wins over a permission cache entry. It never performs a denied Check, then grants the permission in the store, then checks again and expects Allowed=true. That sequence is the scenario this PR exists for, and the test would have caught the stale denial described above. The test also seeds a permCache value that contradicts the denial, so it does not exercise a realistic cache state.

findings.title: Denial cache key built by underscore concatenation can collide
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey joins userUID, action, name and parent with '_' without escaping. Folder and dashboard UIDs may contain underscores, so different tuples can produce the same key (for example name "a_b" with parent "" versus name "a" with parent "b"). A collision would deny a request that should be allowed for up to the TTL. Use an unambiguous separator or a hash of the tuple.
